turns.prompt: Logging out only clears the cookie in the browser; the session itself stays alive on the server. destroySession in lib/auth.js already drops a session but nothing calls it. Please make POST /logout really end the session with it: after logout, anyone who replays the old cookie must get 401 from GET /me. The logout itself still answers 200.
Logout works now: the old cookie is dead after I log out.

The session cookie is called sid, which tells every visitor how the app works. Rename it to notes_session: login must set a cookie with that name (and no sid any more), and the app must read the new cookie back.
Add GET /health that answers 200 with { "status": "ok" } and needs no login.
Add GET /stats for the logged-in user: it answers 200 with { "notes": <how many notes that user has> }.
Add GET /export for the logged-in user: it answers 200 with a JSON array of their notes, each with id, title and body, and sends the header Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="notes.json".

praise.words: Logout works now: the old cookie is dead after I log out.

risk.summary: Renaming the cookie to notes_session, the logout helper still reads the old sid cookie, so logout no longer ends the session.

regression.note: sessionId() in lib/auth.js still reads sid
